items.title: Karnataka finds ethanol blending of up to 31.2% in petrol, seeks explanation from Union government
items.summary: The Karnataka government has alleged that petrol sold by major oil marketing companies in the state contains ethanol in excess of the prescribed 20% blend, with laboratory tests recording levels as high as 31.2%. Food and Civil Supplies Minister Rizwan Arshad, who released the findings at a press conference on Friday, November 6, said the state government had tested 63 petrol samples collected from different parts of Karnataka, including Bengaluru, Kolar, Chikkaballapura, Bengaluru Rural, Ramanagara, Mangaluru and Tumakuru. According to the findings released by the department, samples from Indian Oil Corporation Limited (IOCL), Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited (HPCL), Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited (BPCL), Nayara Energy, Shell and Mangalore Refinery and Petrochemicals Limited (MRPL) showed ethanol content exceeding 20% in several instances. The highest ethanol content recorded was 31.2% in an IOCL petrol sample, followed by 30.5% in an HPCL Power sample. Other samples recorded levels of 27%, 26.5%, 26.1%, 25.5%, 24.2%, 22.6%, 22.4%, 20.8% and 20.6%. The lowest recorded level was 13.5%. items.title: Punjab & Haryana High Court asks Centre to examine whether LPU violence warrants NIA probe
items.summary: The Punjab and Haryana High Court has directed the Central government to examine whether the National Investigation Agency (NIA) needs to take over the ongoing Punjab Police probe into the recent violence and arson at Lovely Professional University (LPU) [Ravi Raj v Union of India & Ors] A bench of Chief Justice of Ashwani Kumar Mishra and Justice Rohit Kapoor passed the order on Wednesday in a Public Interest Litigation (PIL) petition seeking a Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) probe into the violence that broke out after false rumours spread about alleged sexual assault of a female student on LPU campus. The Court noted that the police, during the course of the investigation, has found material which prima facie indicates applicability of the offence of cyber terrorism under Section 66F of the Information Technology Act, 2000. Considering that Section 66F is a scheduled offence under the National Investigation Agency Act, the Court directed the State to forward a report with regard to commissioning of the offence in terms of Section 6 of the NIA Act, to the Central government. Fankaar Live Experiences Pvt. Ltd. & Ors. ]. The order passed by Justice Madhav Jamdar addresses widespread unauthorised commercial exploitation and digital manipulation of her name and image. The ex-parte order directs various defendants, including e-commerce giants, and social media platforms, to immediately halt the rampant misuse of the actor’s name, image, likeness, voice, and signature. Justice Madhav Jamdar Panday’s plea flagged unauthorised merchandise sales, false representations by talent agencies claiming authority to facilitate her professional bookings, and the unlawful circulation of deepfakes. Furthermore, it raised concerns over AI-enabled chatbots actively impersonating Panday, alongside the dissemination of digitally manipulated, highly offensive, and sexually explicit content across various digital platforms like Meta, X Corp, and Reddit. items.title: Allahabad High Court asks its administrative wing to examine plea to streamline caveats in criminal cases
items.summary: The Allahabad High Court recently indicated that its administrative side will examine a plea seeking the introduction of a system to streamline the filing, registration and notification of caveats in criminal proceedings [ Anupriya Agarwal vs State of UP and Another ]. A Division Bench of Justice Rajan Roy and Justice Manjive Shukla was hearing a public interest litigation (PIL) petition that flagged a gap in the Allahabad Hon'ble Court Rules, 1952. The petition filed by advocate Anupriya Agarwal pointed out that these rules did not lay down any specific mechanism for filing, registering, processing or notifying caveats in criminal proceedings such as in bail applications, criminal appeals, etc. Caveat pleas are requests made to a court to hear a party before passing any order in a matter that may affect their interests. The Court observed that while the petition for a formal caveat filing system prima facie raises an important issue concerning access to justice, the subject matter essentially pertains to court procedure. John Does & Ors] Vacation judge Justice Ashish S Chavan also directed the ISPs and platforms to provide the contact details of their designated nodal officers to ensure swift response to such take down requests. Once such request is received, the platforms have to confirm in writing that they will comply with the order on an immediate, real-time basis and that they have systems and persons in place to do so. The film, an adaptation of the Indian epic Ramayana, was released on November 5. It stars Ranbir Kapoor, Sai Pallavi and Yash as Rama, Sita and Ravana respectively. items.summary: The Kerala High Court on Thursday granted anticipatory bail to an additional sessions judge who whose minor son was recently involved in a car crash that killed a scooterist on October 25. Justice Kauser Edappagath passed the order after noting that there was nothing to indicate that the accused judicial officer will not cooperate with the ongoing investigation. "You have searched his house seized everything. This is something affecting the liberty of a person, whether District Judge or anyone. items.title: Supreme Court asks Allahabad High Court to hear Azam Khan's plea against ED arrest on November 16
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Thursday directed the Allahabad High Court to grant priority hearing on November 16 to Samajwadi Party (SP) leader Mohd Azam Khan's plea challenging his arrest by the Enforcement Directorate (ED) immediately after he was released from jail in another case. A bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi said that while Khan's arguments concerning political malice against him might have some substance, it will refrain from expressing any opinion on the merits of the matter and would leave it to the High Court. "There is one ECIR, but 28 cases. Just see the document. This is pure persecution. This Court cannot allow this. Please see page 197. How can anybody file an FIR in 2019 concerning an incident of 2006, when I was out of power?" Senior Advocate Kapil Sibal said on behalf of Khan. "Your argument may have some substance but we do not want to express any opinion," the CJI remarked. The Court, therefore, directed Khan to approach the High Court and directed the High Court to grant priority hearing in the matter.
